newsitem.title: UK: UK lottery winner dies after 20-month binge - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK lottery winner dies after 20-month binge - paper.

text.p: A British former factory worker who scooped a lottery prize worth 11 million pounds ($18.6 million) died after a 20-month binge on cigarettes, drink and takeaway food, the tabloid Sun newspaper said on Tuesday.

It said Ernie Bailey, 63, ignored doctors' advice to stop drinking and smoking and had ballooned to 310 pounds (140 kg) by the time he died in the luxury bungalow he bought after the win in April of last year.
"Poor old Ernie is proof you can't take it with you," the newspaper quoted a family friend as saying.
"He was told time and again to give up fags (cigarettes) because of a heart condition and cut out drink to lose weight. But he loved his pleasures and in the end, they did for him."

Even when it became clear his health was deteriorating Bailey carried on smoking, visiting the local pub and staying up late to watch videos and eat takeaways without taking any exercise, the newspaper said.
